primary_meaning: The Christian believer (or people of God) as a temporary sojourner, pilgrim, or exile on earth whose true citizenship and home are in heaven

alternatives.meaning: The foreigner/resident alien (ger/xenos) who must receive justice, protection, and hospitality as a reflection of God's character and Israel's own experience as strangers in Egypt
Christ himself present in and identified with the needy outsider or guest
The people of God (Israel or the church) living in diaspora or exile status among the nations

notes: The term functions both ethically (OT law of the ger) and spiritually (NT pilgrim identity); the pilgrim/exile motif is the most frequent traditional symbolic application in Christian teaching and spirituality, yet ethical hospitality readings remain equally widespread, especially in modern interpretation. No single exclusive symbolic consensus exists.
